questions.stem: How is a Knowledge Graph (KG) compared to a relational database in I Am Datapedia!?
options: Just as a row is the physical content in a relational database, a Knowledge Graph is the physical content in a graph database
A Knowledge Graph is the index of a relational database
A Knowledge Graph is the schema of a relational database
A Knowledge Graph is a backup of a relational database
A Knowledge Graph is a query language for relational databases
questions.explanation: A row is the physical content in a relational database; likewise a Knowledge Graph is the physical content in a graph database.

options: A hierarchical list of categories
A structured representation of knowledge where entities (nodes) and their relationships (edges) are stored and queried in a graph format
A set of rules that constrain a database schema
A visual chart of company revenue
A collection of unstructured documents
questions.explanation: A Knowledge Graph is a structured representation of knowledge, storing entities as nodes and relationships as edges in a graph format.

questions.stem: A Knowledge Graph is described as the populated version of four things. Which set is correct?
options: Tables, rows, columns and keys
Files, folders, drives and servers
Graph Theory (structure), MetaGraph (metadata), Taxonomies (classification) and Ontologies (rules)
Dashboards, reports, KPIs and OKRs
ETL, ELT, streaming and batch
questions.explanation: Like a relational schema populated with rows, a Knowledge Graph is the populated version of Graph Theory, MetaGraph, Taxonomies and Ontologies.

questions.stem: What does a Knowledge Graph add to the abstract structure that Graph Theory provides?
options: A hierarchical classification
Reasoning rules
A relational schema
Data instances: nodes representing real-world entities and edges representing actual relationships
A programming language
questions.explanation: Graph Theory gives the mathematical structure; the Knowledge Graph adds data instances such as (Person: Alice) -[:Knows]-> (Person: Bob).

questions.stem: What kind of metadata does a Knowledge Graph embed for each node and edge, according to the MetaGraph comparison?
options: Only the primary key
The colour and size of the node
The name of the database administrator
The SQL used to create it
Source, provenance, lineage or confidence scores
questions.explanation: A Knowledge Graph includes metadata such as source, provenance, lineage or confidence scores, for example a 'Knows' edge with Confidence 0.95.

questions.stem: How does a Knowledge Graph relate to a Taxonomy such as Electronics, Laptops, Gaming Laptops?
options: It instantiates the classification by linking specific data entities to their categories, such as a Dell Gaming Laptop belonging to Gaming Laptops
It replaces the taxonomy with a flat list
It stores the taxonomy as a single node
It ignores the taxonomy entirely
It defines the rules by which the taxonomy is built
questions.explanation: The Taxonomy provides a generic hierarchy; the Knowledge Graph maps actual data to it, for example (Product: Dell Gaming Laptop) -[:Belongs To]-> (Category: Gaming Laptops).

questions.stem: In the Knowledge Graph comparison, what does an Ontology define?
options: The physical rows of data
The schema, rules and semantics for entities and relationships, such as 'a Product must Belong To a Category'
The confidence score of every edge
The mathematical definition of a vertex
The storage engine of the graph database
questions.explanation: An Ontology defines the schema, rules and semantics; the Knowledge Graph instantiates that schema with actual data that adheres to those rules.

questions.stem: In the relational-to-graph comparison, an Orders table with columns OrderID, CustomerID and OrderDate corresponds to what in a Knowledge Graph?
options: A single node called Orders with no edges
A taxonomy of order categories
Nodes for Customers and Orders with a Purchases edge between them, such as (Customer: Alice) -[:Purchases {Date: '2023-12-12'}]-> (Order: #12345)
A column called Purchases
An ontology rule that customers must exist
questions.explanation: In the Knowledge Graph, Customers and Orders become nodes and Purchases becomes an edge carrying properties such as the date.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the concepts that a Knowledge Graph is said to integrate closely with and unify?
options: Graph Theory
MetaGraph
Taxonomies
Star schemas
Ontologies
questions.explanation: A Knowledge Graph integrates closely with Graph Theory, MetaGraph, Taxonomies and Ontologies, acting as a unifying framework; star schemas are not part of that list.

questions.stem: In a relational database, what is the state of the schema (tables, columns, constraints) before rows are added, and what is the equivalent in the graph world?
options: The schema is full of default data; the Knowledge Graph is likewise pre-filled
The schema does not exist until rows arrive; the Knowledge Graph creates its structure on the fly
The schema is locked; the Knowledge Graph is read-only
The schema is deleted; the Knowledge Graph is archived
The schema is empty until populated with rows; similarly the Knowledge Graph is the populated version of the graph structure, metadata, classification and rules
questions.explanation: A relational schema is empty until rows populate it, and in the same way the Knowledge Graph is the populated version of Graph Theory, MetaGraph, Taxonomies and Ontologies.
